A.strongest_objection: A protocol could appear to work only because the analyst supplied the unread companion word as a hidden success flag.
A.design_response: Every proposed operation and herald must use reader-accessible records. Verify both rules at every reachable event, including refusals. Resolving unread names can give an upper bound only by a proof that applies to the original unresolved protocol. Check both reader placements and complete surviving target maps.

B.strongest_objection: A direct shared name between the two live ends does not witness their binary birth under the actual growth law. Without a third holder meeting both, the proposed case can only give separate unary births with constant extension counts.
B.design_response: Keep the original roster as a negative control. Enroll a separate spent common witness, check the actual old and fresh names in the funded join, the minimum number of holder meetings to the recorded event, and the old-event change. Separate feasible choices, completion counts and alternative sampling schemes.

B.strongest_objection: The spent witness changes the old relation as well as making a new kind of birth possible. A comparison between different starting arrangements cannot establish that the birth changed an old event.
B.design_response: Compare the same marked event before and after growth inside each arrangement. Verify the exact two consumed loose names with the ordinary engine and the intervening holder count, keep inherited weights as a match, and reserve arbitrary separation for a proof. The fixed-support theorem, language converse, initial prior and feasibility query have separate hypotheses.
